title: Balanced Freekeh Bowl
subtitle: with Baked Fennel and Hemp Seeds
description: Load up on goodness with this nourishing grain bowl. Think nutty freekeh, good-for-you kale and sweet baked fennel and tomatoes. Dotted with nuts and seeds, it's taste and texture combined.

steps.text: Cook freekeh: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line 2 oven trays with baking paper. Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Cook the freekeh, partially covered, for 18-20 mins until tender. Drain.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, trim the fennel and cut lengthwise into 2cm-thick wedges, then finely chop the fennel fronds, if any. Remove the tough inner stems from the kale, then coarsely chop the leaves. Coarsely chop the olives. Thinly slice 2 garlic cloves.

Bake fennel and tomatoes: Put the fennel, tomatoes and garlic on a lined tray and scatter over the fennel fronds. Drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper and turn to coat. Bake on the upper oven shelf for 15-18 mins until golden and tender. Press down lightly on the tomatoes to release a little juice.

Toast nuts and seeds: Meanwhile, put the almonds and hemp seeds on the remaining lined tray. Bake on the lower shelf for 3-5 mins until golden. Put the kale in a large bowl, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil and 1 tsp red wine vinegar and season with salt. Using your hands, massage the leaves for 1 min or until softened (see Kitchen 101).

Serve up: Add the freekeh, olives, nuts and seeds, fennel mixture and pan juices to the kale and toss to combine. Put 1 tbs olive oil and 2 tsp red wine vinegar in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and whisk to combine. Drizzle the dressing over the freekeh mixture and toss to combine. Divide among bowls and enjoy!

Kitchen 101: Yes, you read it correctly – kale needs to be massaged! This is a really important step because it helps to break down the tough fibres, making it tender and easier to eat. Gently pinch and squeeze the leaves until they start to shrink, soften and darken a little.
